final_candidates.decision_summary: V153 lies in domain II near the fusion-loop region; a conservative hydrophobic Val-to-Met change plausibly improves fusion/membrane interactions with low structural risk.
T231 is in the domain I–II linker region; a small hydrophobic substitution could stabilize interdomain packing and virion assembly, though the fitness benefit is uncertain.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available, so additional rounds cannot improve the prior-based ranking and are unlikely to change the Top-3.

history.rationale: Position 153 sits adjacent to the E glycosylation site (N154) in domain II; the V->M change is a documented ZIKV American-lineage adaptation associated with enhanced replication in vertebrate and mosquito cells.

Position 153 lies in E domain II near the fusion-loop region; conservative hydrophobic substitution plausibly improves membrane fusion efficiency and replication fitness without large structural risk.
Domain I/II hinge-region substitution that can modestly alter conformational dynamics and fusion-loop exposure, potentially improving entry efficiency.
Residue 231 sits in a loop between domain I and II; a small hydrophobic change could stabilize interdomain packing, but benefit is uncertain.
Residue 155 neighbors the conserved N154 glycosylation sequon; D->N may create or shift an N-linked glycan, altering particle assembly and cell entry.

D155 is adjacent to the N154 glycosylation motif region; loss of glycosylation usually reduces fitness, but loss of the acidic side chain alone (conserving Asn at 154) may be tolerated—downgraded due to risk.
Domain III surface lysine near receptor-binding region; conservative charge-preserving change may tune receptor interaction without structural penalty.
K373R in domain III is a very conservative change with low expected fitness effect; retained only as a low-confidence candidate.
